+    def _is_unrollable_all_call(self, call):
+        """Return True if the given ast.Call is a call to the builtin
+        ``all`` with a single generator expression or list comprehension
+        as its only argument, and can therefore be safely "unrolled"
+        into an equivalent for-loop to provide a much more useful
+        failure message (see issue #5062 for the rationale).
+
+        ``any`` is intentionally not handled here: unlike ``all``, a
+        failing ``any`` call cannot be attributed to a single element
+        of the iterable (it fails only when *none* of the elements
+        satisfy the predicate), so unrolling it would not provide a
+        more useful failure message.
+        """
+        return (
+            isinstance(call.func, ast.Name)
+            and call.func.id == "all"
+            and len(call.args) == 1
+            and not call.keywords
+            and isinstance(call.args[0], (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp))
+            and not any(
+                getattr(gen, "is_async", 0) for gen in call.args[0].generators
+            )
+        )
+
+    def _assert_expr_to_stmt(self, expr, lineno, col_offset, dest_statements):
+        """Build the statements required to assert *expr* is truthy and
+        append them to *dest_statements*.
+
+        This performs the same job as :meth:`visit_Assert` but instead
+        of operating on ``self.statements`` (and resetting
+        ``self.variables``/``self.variable_counter``/... as
+        :meth:`visit_Assert` does for a top level assert), it appends
+        the generated statements to *dest_statements*.  This allows the
+        helper to be used to build the body of a for-loop when
+        "unrolling" calls such as ``all(x for x in iterable)`` while
+        continuing to share variable names/counters with the enclosing
+        assertion being rewritten.
+        """
+        save_statements = self.statements
+        save_on_failure = self.on_failure
+        self.statements = dest_statements
+        self.on_failure = []
+        self.push_format_context()
+        top_condition, explanation = self.visit(expr)
+        body = self.on_failure
+        negation = ast.UnaryOp(ast.Not(), top_condition)
+        self.statements.append(ast.If(negation, body, []))
+        explanation = "assert " + explanation
+        template = ast.BinOp(ast.Str(""), ast.Add(), ast.Str(explanation))
+        msg = self.pop_format_context(template)
+        fmt = self.helper("_format_explanation", msg)
+        err_name = ast.Name("AssertionError", ast.Load())
+        exc = ast_Call(err_name, [fmt], [])
+        if sys.version_info[0] >= 3:
+            raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None)
+        else:
+            raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None, None)
+        body.append(raise_)
+        for stmt in dest_statements:
+            set_location(stmt, lineno, col_offset)
+        self.statements = save_statements
+        self.on_failure = save_on_failure
+
+    def _unroll_all_call(self, call):
+        """"Unroll" a call such as ``all(x for x in iterable)`` (or using
+        a list comprehension) into an equivalent for-loop which asserts
+        the predicate for each item individually, so that a failure
+        points at the specific item (and its own repr/explanation)
+        instead of just reporting that ``all(...)`` returned False.
+
+        Returns a ``(res, expl)`` tuple, just like the other ``visit_*``
+        methods, where *res* is always a true-ish node (if we get this
+        far without an assertion firing, the original call would have
+        returned True) and *expl* is empty, since the real explanation
+        (if any) will already have been raised by the unrolled
+        for-loop.
+        """
+        gen_exp = call.args[0]
+        elt = gen_exp.elt
+        inner_body = []
+        self._assert_expr_to_stmt(elt, call.lineno, call.col_offset, inner_body)
+        for comp in reversed(gen_exp.generators):
+            for cond in reversed(comp.ifs):
+                inner_body = [
+                    ast.If(cond, inner_body, [])
+                ]
+            for_loop = ast.For(
+                target=comp.target, iter=comp.iter, body=inner_body, orelse=[]
+            )
+            inner_body = [for_loop]
+        self.statements.extend(inner_body)
+        return _NameConstant(True), ""
+
